Six-case hydro-topological simulation explorer

Recorded source-routing results + live finite-buffer stress test. CDO and five Southeast Asian analogues. Fully offline.

Model boundary: These are report-derived coarse network models with synthetic inputs and parameters, not mapped flood forecasts. A tick is not an hour; spill is not flood depth. CDO is not a demonstrated Lapasan inundation node. The six PDFs do not contain complete georeferenced drainage networks.

1. Choose a recorded source-routing case

This demonstration subset uses equal source weights, all source groups active, unit logical-link delays, zero ordinary link memory and realization 0. The full 1,152-scenario grammar, area sensitivity, graph alternatives and counterexamples are in the reproducibility package.

2. Change the hypothetical receiving capacity and buffer

Each observation is a standalone experiment: spills at different probes must not be added together. Positive capacity is given enough extra ticks to drain the remaining buffer. A closed outlet retains water rather than deleting it.

3. See arrivals and buffer overflow

Solid line: stored amount. Vertical bars: spill during that tick. Dashed horizontal line: available buffer. The marker is a timeline guide, not a moving flood front on a map.

4. Source-constrained coarse graph and evidence limit

How to interpret the experiment

Structure determines which routes contributions share. Pulse timing and routing functions determine when they meet. A capacity/buffer threshold determines whether this defined model spills. Similar topology does not guarantee identical output when those parameters differ.

Three useful comparisons: change source starting-time spread while keeping capacity and buffer fixed; compare neutral and active storage in Manado/Huong; compare the Huong urban point with its downstream receiver to see why Bo is not added before Hue.

Do not turn these values into real annual flood probabilities. No measured storm frequency, channel capacity, water level, local drain geometry or Lapasan flood footprint was fitted. The larger experiment contains negative findings and counterexamples as well as positive mean effects.

Source keys and graph definitions are in the accompanying methods/results report. This viewer uses source-tagged routed series generated by the bundled Python model; its live buffer update uses the same equations.
